subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept this grouped set of privileged GitHub Action revisions after the four deterministic SHA assertions are repaired?
rationale: The revisions are immutable and no specific malicious change was found, but they replace third-party code running at credential, publishing, security-scanning, repository-mutation, and Codex-agent boundaries; that trust decision belongs to human owners.

options.title: Repair and audit the batch
options.body: Synchronize all SHA assertions, rebase, validate the exact head, and accept the reviewed revisions together.

options.title: Split privileged updates
options.body: Move credential-, publishing-, scanning-, maintenance-, and Codex-bearing actions into smaller independently reviewed pull requests.

options.title: Pause the update
options.body: Retain the current pins if the combined supply-chain review cost is not worthwhile now.

recommendation.title: Repair and audit the batch
recommendation.body: Synchronize all SHA assertions, rebase, validate the exact head, and accept the reviewed revisions together.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main provenance is on the central CI workflow and exact-SHA guard suite that coordinate this grouped update.
